A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLASMA study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VenusX benchmark experiments, alignment analyses, sensitivity studies and biological case studies in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, expanded baseline analyses and sequence-similarity diagnostics.

M1.justification: Sections 2–5 retain the cost network, parameter-free variant, Sinkhorn procedure, similarity scoring and BCE-plus-LML objective. Clarifications and experimental component removals do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VenusX motifs, binding sites and active sites under interpolation and extrapolation, alongside the same biological case studies. Appendix L reanalyzes existing test pairs; moving extrapolation results into Table 1 adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds TM-align and Foldseek to the score-distribution and structural-similarity comparisons, where v1 evaluated four embedding-based methods. Both were already benchmark comparators elsewhere. The summary-table label Backbone corresponds to the existing CosineSim comparator.

E3.justification: New Table 10 introduces controls removing LML or confidence-weight correction. Appendix L adds a diagnostic relating alignment scores to aligned-residue sequence identity and coverage. Existing benchmark splits, sampling, hyperparameters and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds systematic component ablations across seven backbones and three tasks, testing the contributions of LML and weight correction. Appendix L adds sequence-identity and coverage diagnostics, while Figure 3 expands the existing structural-similarity analysis. Earlier sensitivity studies and case studies remain; Appendix H enlarges existing cases rather than introducing new ones.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 1, 42 and 100, report means and standard deviations across three seeds, and retain Figure 2's standard-error reporting. Added results follow existing uncertainty-reporting practices; no increased run count or new statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: New results include component-ablation scores, TM-align/Foldseek diagnostic comparisons and sequence-similarity findings. Table 10 reports ESM2 motif ROC-AUC of 0.93 for PLASMA-PF versus 0.44 without weight correction. The full benchmark tables retain their scores. v2 Table 5 also corrects swapped binding/active summary values: TM-align ROC-AUC changes from 0.94/0.87 in v1 Table 1 to 0.87/0.94, matching the retained detailed tables.

T1.justification: The OT objective and constraints, model and loss equations, and Appendix B complexity argument remain unchanged. The new sequence-similarity description introduces a standard empirical measurement, not a new mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's claim to be the first deep learning framework and explicitly includes non-sequential motif alignment in the introduction's contributions. The central claims about accuracy, efficiency, interpretability and the training-free variant remain.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds interpretations of LML as specialization with possible extrapolation costs and weight correction as protection against fragmented matches. Appendix L attributes high scores to structural correspondence and claims independence from global homology and unintended leakage. These extend the earlier interpretations without replacing the central explanation.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement explicitly reports releasing source code and trained models under an open-source license, with reproduction instructions in the repository. v1 already linked the implementation. Hardware, backbone configurations and documented hyperparameters remain unchanged; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds ActSeek, eplsaPALIGN and Pellizzoni et al.'s learnable graph matching work. It distinguishes PLASMA's explicit local mappings from prior OT-based substitution-cost learning, accompanying the removal of the broad first-framework claim. Existing cited approaches remain.

P1.justification: v2 refines terminology around local structural motifs, rewrites the contribution and related-work paragraphs, and reorganizes Section 6.2 around extrapolation. It adds an appendix roadmap and reproducibility, ethics and LLM-use statements. Most methodological prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redesigned to include six methods. Table 1 redisplays extrapolation results with LMS, while appendix summaries add relative-percentage annotations. New ablation and threshold tables, sequence-similarity plots, and an enlarged, rearranged version of Figure 5 materially expand the visual presentation. Existing appendix plots are retained, often at higher resolution.

improvement.justification: The added ablations and expanded structural-similarity comparisons strengthen empirical support, while corrected interpolation summaries and more accurate positioning against prior OT work improve reliability. These provide a modest net benefit to the retained study. However, Appendix L overstates its diagnostic as establishing absence of data leakage, and some ablation interpretations are broader than Table 10 supports.
